requirements.section: Business ERP — Shared Architecture and Delivery Standards / Repository and responsibilities
requirements.text: Use business-erp/frontend and business-erp/backend, with root-level operational configuration and documentation.

requirements.section: Business ERP — Shared Architecture and Delivery Standards / Repository and responsibilities
requirements.text: - Frontend: components/common, forms, tables, charts, modals and layout; pages by business module; layouts, services, hooks, context, utils, constants, validations and routes.

requirements.section: Business ERP — Shared Architecture and Delivery Standards / Repository and responsibilities

requirements.section: Business ERP — Shared Architecture and Delivery Standards / Repository and responsibilities
requirements.text: - Routers handle transport and authorization dependencies. Pydantic schemas handle request and response validation.

requirements.section: Business ERP — Shared Architecture and Delivery Standards / Repository and responsibilities
requirements.text: - Repositories handle persistence; services enforce business rules and coordinate transactions. Avoid repositories that silently commit.

requirements.section: Business ERP — Shared Architecture and Delivery Standards / Repository and responsibilities
requirements.text: - The initiating service owns the database transaction. Commit related document, stock, financial and audit records together.

requirements.section: Business ERP — Shared Architecture and Delivery Standards / Repository and responsibilities
requirements.text: - Background workers handle exports, reminders and alerts after commit. They must not be the only mechanism guaranteeing stock or financial integrity.

requirements.section: Business ERP — Shared Architecture and Delivery Standards / Repository and responsibilities
requirements.text: Document APIs with FastAPI OpenAPI and meaningful response models.

requirements.section: Business ERP — Shared Architecture and Delivery Standards / Data and transaction invariants
requirements.text: 1. Use PostgreSQL NUMERIC and Python Decimal for money, quantities and rates with explicitly chosen scales. Exchange decimal values as strings where JavaScript arithmetic could lose precision.

requirements.section: Business ERP — Shared Architecture and Delivery Standards / Data and transaction invariants
requirements.text: 2. Store dated business events and UTC timestamps. Apply the configured business timezone when grouping days and generating schedules.

requirements.section: Business ERP — Shared Architecture and Delivery Standards / Data and transaction invariants
requirements.text: 3. Give operational documents unique business-scoped numbers; use internal immutable identifiers for relationships.

requirements.section: Business ERP — Shared Architecture and Delivery Standards / Data and transaction invariants
requirements.text: 4. Snapshot transaction prices, discounts, taxes, unit conversion factors and costs. Later edits to master data must not rewrite history.

requirements.section: Business ERP — Shared Architecture and Delivery Standards / Data and transaction invariants
requirements.text: 5. Keep finalized stock and financial history immutable. Corrections use linked reversals, returns or adjustment documents.

requirements.section: Business ERP — Shared Architecture and Delivery Standards / Data and transaction invariants
requirements.text: 6. Require balanced journal entries for financial events. Validate balance at the posting boundary and prevent later direct edits.

requirements.section: Business ERP — Shared Architecture and Delivery Standards / Data and transaction invariants
requirements.text: 7. Reject negative stock unless an authorized administrator explicitly enables it. Audit policy changes and enforce the same rules across every entry point.

requirements.section: Business ERP — Shared Architecture and Delivery Standards / Data and transaction invariants
requirements.text: 8. Prevent concurrent overselling with transaction locking or another demonstrated equivalent; a frontend stock check is insufficient.

requirements.section: Business ERP — Shared Architecture and Delivery Standards / Data and transaction invariants
requirements.text: 9. Use idempotency keys on posting/finalization, payments, returns and production completion. Persist the request fingerprint and result; reject conflicting reuse.

requirements.section: Business ERP — Shared Architecture and Delivery Standards / Data and transaction invariants
requirements.text: 10. Preserve transaction references and actor identity across documents, inventory movements, batch movements, journal entries and audit records.

requirements.section: Business ERP — Shared Architecture and Delivery Standards / Data and transaction invariants
requirements.text: 11. Make stock balances and party balances reconcile to their authoritative movement and financial records.

requirements.section: Business ERP — Shared Architecture and Delivery Standards / Data and transaction invariants
requirements.text: 12. Verify object access and module/action permissions on the backend. Hidden buttons do not authorize requests.

requirements.section: Business ERP — Shared Architecture and Delivery Standards / Proposed domain conventions
requirements.text: Use a stock transaction header and immutable movement lines. Record product, warehouse, base-unit quantity, unit cost, value, batch where relevant, source document, effective date and actor. Maintain stock balances transactionally as an acceleration layer.

requirements.section: Business ERP — Shared Architecture and Delivery Standards / Proposed domain conventions
requirements.text: Keep stock allocation separate from valuation. Physical FIFO selects older stock; FEFO selects the earliest eligible expiry. The financial valuation method is a separate business setting. Do not silently change it after posted activity.

requirements.section: Business ERP — Shared Architecture and Delivery Standards / Proposed domain conventions
requirements.text: Use journal entries with at least two journal lines, account, debit or credit, source document and posting date. Entries must balance at configured precision. Business documents reference their posting records.

requirements.section: Business ERP — Shared Architecture and Delivery Standards / Proposed domain conventions
requirements.text: Customer and supplier ledgers are controlled views or subledgers backed by posted financial events. Do not maintain an unrelated editable balance field as the source of truth.

requirements.section: Business ERP — Shared Architecture and Delivery Standards / Proposed domain conventions
requirements.text: Recommended document flow: draft → approved where configured → posted/finalized. Document cancellation either discards an unposted draft or creates a linked reversal of a posted document. Define the exact allowed transitions for each module.

requirements.section: Business ERP — Shared Architecture and Delivery Standards / API conventions
requirements.text: All phase routes below are proposed contracts under /api/v1. Resolve names consistently in OpenAPI during implementation.

requirements.section: Business ERP — Shared Architecture and Delivery Standards / API conventions
requirements.text: - Use bounded pagination, explicit filters and stable ordering on lists.

requirements.section: Business ERP — Shared Architecture and Delivery Standards / API conventions
requirements.text: - Return consistent validation and business-error envelopes with a request identifier.

requirements.section: Business ERP — Shared Architecture and Delivery Standards / API conventions
requirements.text: - Use 401 for missing/invalid authentication, 403 for forbidden actions, 404 for inaccessible/missing resources, and 409 for state or idempotency conflicts where appropriate.

requirements.section: Business ERP — Shared Architecture and Delivery Standards / API conventions
requirements.text: - Validate quantities, payment allocation totals, dates, statuses and required fields on the server.

requirements.section: Business ERP — Shared Architecture and Delivery Standards / API conventions
requirements.text: - Restrict export, approval, reversal and configuration operations explicitly.

requirements.section: Business ERP — Shared Architecture and Delivery Standards / API conventions
requirements.text: - Version important updates or lock records to reject stale edits.

requirements.section: Business ERP — Shared Architecture and Delivery Standards / API conventions
requirements.text: - Do not expose stack traces, credentials or token values in errors or logs.

requirements.section: Business ERP — Shared Architecture and Delivery Standards / UI standards
requirements.text: Provide a responsive dashboard layout, sidebar, top bar, reusable forms, searchable paginated tables, date and dropdown filters, confirmation dialogs, loading and empty states, useful validation, toast notifications, accessible focus behavior, and persisted light/dark mode.

requirements.section: Business ERP — Shared Architecture and Delivery Standards / UI standards
requirements.text: Every action must call a real API or clearly display that it is unavailable. Disable duplicate submission while requests are pending, then display persisted results from the API. Keep accounting terminology clear for shop operators.

requirements.section: Business ERP — Shared Architecture and Delivery Standards / Financial integration contract
requirements.text: Define a posting service that accepts a typed business event and source identifier and returns a posting reference. Validate account mappings, period status and idempotency before stock or financial mutations become final.

requirements.text: Typical events include opening_inventory, stock_adjustment, goods_received, supplier_invoice, sale_posted, payment_received, payment_sent, sales_return, purchase_return, production_consumed and production_completed.

requirements.text: Implement end-to-end purchasing, receiving, wholesale/retail billing, POS, settlements and returns with immediate, consistent inventory and financial effects.

requirements.section: Phase 4 — Purchases and Sales / Prerequisites
requirements.text: Phases 1–3 pass. Product/party/location records, inventory allocation, idempotency and the balanced posting kernel work.

requirements.section: Phase 4 — Purchases and Sales / Purchasing scope

requirements.section: Phase 4 — Purchases and Sales / Purchasing scope
requirements.text: Track ordered, received, returned and remaining quantities. Reject over-receipt unless a configured authorized tolerance permits it. Allocate landed purchase costs by a documented rule.

requirements.section: Phase 4 — Purchases and Sales / Sales scope
requirements.text: Support sales invoices, a fast POS screen, wholesale/retail price selection, cash/credit sales, partial/full payments, discounts, minimum price rules, cancellation, customer/product history and profit per invoice/product.

requirements.section: Phase 4 — Purchases and Sales / Sales scope
requirements.text: Support cash, bank transfer and configurable payment channels. Validate credit limits, available stock and batch eligibility. Provide printable invoices.

requirements.section: Phase 4 — Purchases and Sales / Sales scope
requirements.text: A credit sale increases receivables; cash increases only when a payment is actually posted. Do not treat an invoice as a receipt of cash.

Phase 5 — Accounting / Backend work
requirements.text: Implement account types, posting restrictions, mapping validation and period locks. Require every journal to balance at currency precision, with exactly one debit/credit direction per line and valid posting accounts.

requirements.section: Phase 5 — Accounting / Backend work
requirements.text: A transfer debits the receiving cash/bank account and credits the sending account; it does not create income. Allocate receipts/payments without exceeding available amounts. Keep advances visible as unapplied balances until correctly allocated.

requirements.section: Phase 5 — Accounting / Backend work
requirements.text: Stage opening balances, validate total debits equal credits and post them once. Distinguish prior opening balances from ordinary revenue. Do not duplicate stock, customer or supplier openings entered in earlier phases.

requirements.section: Phase 5 — Accounting / Backend work
requirements.text: Produce statements from posted data with a documented account mapping. Balance sheet assets must reconcile to liabilities plus equity, including current earnings. Derive cash flow from cash movements with configured classification; profit is not a substitute for cash flow.

requirements.section: Phase 5 — Accounting / Backend work
requirements.text: Use as-of dates for aging and statements, including reversals/allocations effective by that date. Protect finalized documents and closed periods. Audit journal posting, mappings, opening balances, reconciliation and period changes.

requirements.section: Phase 5 — Accounting / Frontend work
requirements.text: Build accounting navigation, account tree, journal editor, cash/bank books, party ledgers, outstanding invoice views, allocation dialogs, expense forms, reconciliation matching and statement screens.

requirements.section: Phase 5 — Accounting / Frontend work
requirements.text: Show debits/credits, opening/running/closing balances and statement filters clearly. Display unpaid invoices separately from cash movements. Show unallocated advances and block incomplete journals before submission, with server validation as final authority.

requirements.section: Phase 5 — Accounting / Acceptance checks
requirements.text: - Unbalanced journals fail and leave no committed lines.

requirements.section: Phase 5 — Accounting / Acceptance checks
requirements.text: - Credit sales/purchases affect AR/AP without falsely changing cash.

requirements.section: Phase 5 — Accounting / Acceptance checks
requirements.text: - A partial payment reduces the correct invoice balance once.

requirements.section: Phase 5 — Accounting / Acceptance checks
requirements.text: - A cash-to-bank transfer preserves total liquid assets and creates no income.

requirements.section: Phase 5 — Accounting / Acceptance checks
requirements.text: - Aged balances match an as-of-date fixture even after later payments.

requirements.section: Phase 5 — Accounting / Acceptance checks
requirements.text: - Party subledgers reconcile to control accounts.

requirements.section: Phase 5 — Accounting / Acceptance checks
requirements.text: - Trial balance debits equal credits; the balance sheet equation holds.

requirements.section: Phase 5 — Accounting / Acceptance checks
requirements.text: - Repeated opening balance or payment requests do not duplicate postings.

requirements.section: Phase 5 — Accounting / Acceptance checks
requirements.text: - Bank statement duplicates cannot be imported twice without explicit handling.

requirements.section: Phase 5 — Accounting / Acceptance checks
requirements.text: - Closed-period backdating and unauthorized reopening fail.

requirements.section: Phase 5 — Accounting / Deliverables and exit criteria
requirements.text: Deliver a connected accounting workspace, documented posting/account mappings, reconciliations, financial statements and integrity verification. Exit only when operational subledgers, inventory valuation and the GL reconcile for the agreed reference dataset.

requirements.section: Phase 6 — Manufacturing / Goal
requirements.text: Plan daily or weekly production, consume raw materials, produce traceable finished batches, capture quality outcomes and calculate actual production costs.

requirements.section: Phase 6 — Manufacturing / Functional scope

requirements.section: Phase 6 — Manufacturing / Functional scope
requirements.text: Every finished batch has a unique business-scoped identifier, product, manufacturing/production date, optional expiry, produced quantity, consumed material references, production cost and status. Show remaining, sold, returned and damaged quantities through linked inventory events.

Phase 6 — Manufacturing / Backend work
requirements.text: Validate BOM units, positive quantities, yields and references. Block circular dependencies for assemblies and snapshot the approved BOM on released orders so later changes do not alter existing plans.

requirements.section: Phase 6 — Manufacturing / Backend work
requirements.text: Allow documented partial consumption and partial output. Deduplicate schedule-generated orders using schedule occurrence identity; restarting a worker must not create duplicate Friday orders.

requirements.section: Phase 6 — Manufacturing / Backend work
requirements.text: Consume the selected raw material batches at their historical inventory cost. Move material value into work in progress. Accumulate approved labor/overhead without recording the same expense twice. Use documented absorption or allocation rules.

requirements.section: Phase 6 — Manufacturing / Backend work
requirements.text: On completion, move eligible output cost from work in progress to finished inventory. Define normal waste, abnormal loss, rework and scrap treatment explicitly. Prevent division by zero, overshooting remaining planned quantities without approval and completion with unresolved required costs/checks.

requirements.section: Phase 6 — Manufacturing / Backend work
requirements.text: Keep rejected or quarantined goods out of sellable stock until released. Record material and output links so a raw material batch can be traced to every affected finished batch and sale.

requirements.section: Phase 6 — Manufacturing / Backend work
requirements.text: Batch profitability is based on attributable revenue, cost and recorded losses; unsold stock is not recognized as sales revenue.

requirements.section: Phase 6 — Manufacturing / Frontend work
requirements.text: Build BOM editor/version history, production calendar, daily production screen, material availability panel, manufacturing order detail, consumption form, output/batch form, labor/overhead capture, quality checklist and batch traceability view.

requirements.section: Phase 6 — Manufacturing / Frontend work
requirements.text: Show planned versus actual quantities and costs, remaining material, accepted/rejected output, batch expiry and order status. Provide clear controlled actions for release, consume, inspect and complete.

requirements.section: Phase 6 — Manufacturing / Acceptance checks
requirements.text: - Releasing an order snapshots the correct BOM version.

requirements.section: Phase 6 — Manufacturing / Acceptance checks
requirements.text: - Production is blocked when required materials are unavailable.

requirements.section: Phase 6 — Manufacturing / Acceptance checks
requirements.text: - Consuming materials reduces the right raw batches and posts work-in-progress value.

requirements.section: Phase 6 — Manufacturing / Acceptance checks
requirements.text: - A completed batch increases eligible finished stock exactly once.

requirements.section: Phase 6 — Manufacturing / Acceptance checks
requirements.text: - Partial production retains remaining quantities and unfinished work-in-progress value.

requirements.section: Phase 6 — Manufacturing / Acceptance checks
requirements.text: - Labor/overhead allocation reconciles to source costs without duplication.

requirements.section: Phase 6 — Manufacturing / Acceptance checks
requirements.text: - Rejected output remains unavailable for sale.

requirements.section: Phase 6 — Manufacturing / Acceptance checks
requirements.text: - Traceability connects supplier receipt → raw batch → manufacturing order → finished batch → sale.

requirements.section: Phase 6 — Manufacturing / Acceptance checks
requirements.text: - A recurring Friday schedule generates one order per configured occurrence.

requirements.section: Phase 6 — Manufacturing / Acceptance checks
requirements.text: - Failed completion rolls back inventory, journal, status and batch updates.

requirements.section: Phase 6 — Manufacturing / Acceptance checks
requirements.text: - Concurrent or repeated completion cannot create duplicate finished batches.

requirements.section: Phase 6 — Manufacturing / Deliverables and exit criteria
requirements.text: Deliver connected production planning and execution, cost and quality workflows, batch genealogy, migrations and scenario evidence. Exit when material usage, finished quantities, wastage and accounting values reconcile for a representative production run.

requirements.section: Phase 7 — Reports and Analytics / Goal
requirements.text: Provide accurate business visibility through dashboards, inventory/financial/manufacturing reports and shareable PDF/Excel exports.

requirements.section: Phase 7 — Reports and Analytics / Prerequisites
requirements.text: Phases 1–6 pass. Underlying operational and accounting transactions reconcile. Agree on metric definitions and date behavior before implementing charts.

requirements.section: Phase 7 — Reports and Analytics / Dashboard scope
requirements.text: Show total products, stock quantity/value, today's sales/purchases, cash received, credit sales, customer receivables, supplier payables, expenses, gross/net profit, production summary, low/out-of-stock items and recent transactions.

requirements.section: Phase 7 — Reports and Analytics / Dashboard scope
requirements.text: Support daily, weekly, monthly and yearly views, date ranges and relevant warehouse/product/party filters. Label invoice-based metrics separately from cash-based metrics. Mixed units must not be added into a misleading single physical quantity.

requirements.text: Verify the complete ERP as an integrated system, improve measured bottlenecks and prepare a repeatable deployment and recovery process.

requirements.text: Phases 1–7 pass their individual checks. All required workflows use connected APIs and persisted data. Maintain a list of unresolved issues and production configuration decisions.

requirements.section: Phase 8 — Testing and Optimization / Prerequisites

requirements.section: Phase 8 — Testing and Optimization / Optimization work
requirements.text: Use representative data volumes and agree on expected concurrency/response targets. Capture baseline measurements before adding indexes, eager loading, cache or aggregates.

requirements.section: Phase 8 — Testing and Optimization / Optimization work
requirements.text: Review query plans, N+1 access, slow reports, payload size, stock-lock duration, worker throughput and frontend rendering. Preserve audit, transaction and accounting controls while improving performance. Re-run only relevant benchmarks after changes.

requirements.section: Phase 8 — Testing and Optimization / Security and operational preparation
requirements.text: Review password/token handling, CORS, permissions, file upload validation, export authorization, rate limiting, secret management, dependency findings and log redaction.

requirements.text: Create environment-specific configuration, HTTPS/reverse-proxy setup as needed, database migration procedure, health checks, monitoring and alerts. Keep credentials outside source control.

requirements.section: Phase 8 — Testing and Optimization / Security and operational preparation
requirements.text: Back up database and required attachments, document retention objectives and prove a restore. Record recovery-time/recovery-point objectives agreed with the business rather than inventing guarantees.

requirements.section: Phase 8 — Testing and Optimization / Security and operational preparation
requirements.text: Provide a deployment runbook with preflight validation, backup, migration, application/worker startup, readiness checks, smoke tests and rollback/recovery actions. Treat data migrations as potentially non-reversible; an application rollback must not assume automatic schema rollback.
